mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 6% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production and employment both increase, it indicates strong economic activity, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts reflect strong consumer demand, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPI leads to negative S&P 500 returns due to potential rate hikes.
failure_condition: If inflation is high but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales and low unemployment indicate strong economic demand, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies are positive but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth during late expansion signals continued economic strength, positively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative.
